stem: Meera, a Class 6 student in Pune, often falls sick with infections. Her grandmother says she must eat more amla, guava and oranges because these foods 'protect the body'. What is the main reason such foods are called protective nutrients?

options.text: They give the body a large amount of energy for playing and running.
They contain vitamins and minerals that help the body fight and prevent diseases.
They build and repair body muscles like dals and paneer do.
They add bulk to the food and help remove undigested waste.

teacher.key_rationale: Amla, guava and oranges are rich in Vitamin C; vitamins and minerals are protective nutrients because they help prevent deficiency diseases and disorders (e.g., Vitamin C prevents scurvy). A describes energy-giving foods (carbohydrates/fats), C describes body-building foods (proteins), and D describes roughage, none of which is the protective role asked for.
